newsitem.title: JAPAN: Argentina-Chile mine treaty seen early in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Argentina-Chile mine treaty seen early in 1997.

text.p: A mining treaty between Argentina and Chile, originally expected in the fall of this year, is likely to be signed in the first quarter of 1997, Argentina's Under-Secretary for Mining Daniel Meilan said on Wednesday.

He attributed the delays to political factors, including changes in the Chilean cabinet and the recent conclusion of a free-trade pact between Chile and Mercosur, a Latin American customs union that includes Argentina and Brazil.

The Argentina-Chile treaty would promote integration of mining activities in the countries by linking communications and infrastructure and allowing greater freedom of movement of people and equipment across the border, he said.
He identified eight areas along the Argentine-Chilean border with significant resource potential where development could be promoted through greater integration.
Protocols on two of the areas were expected to be signed within the next 15 days, he added, confirming comments in Toronto on Tuesday by Chilean mining minister Benjamin Teplizky.
One protocol involves the Pachon and Los Pelambres projects.
